title: The Cost of Exposing Large Institutional Orders to Electronic Liquidity Providers
authors: Robert H. Battalio; Brian C. Hatch; Mehmet Saglam
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Table 10: one treated client (ClientID C58) that stops routing to ELPs after 2011-03-18.
eligible_reason: No staggered adoption. The only DiD (Table10.R) compares one client (C58) that stops sourcing ELP liquidity after a single date (2011-03-18) with other clients: felm(IS ~ TreatedPost + FracTrBODP + FracTrODP + FracTrPasLit + PartRate + InvPrice + IvlMidVol + FracDur + IvlTvr | Ticker + date + ClientID | 0 | Ticker + ClientID) on parent orders. One treated unit and one adoption date, an extra Ticker FE beyond unit and time, and order-level time-varying controls in both columns. The other tables are order-level regressions on continuous ELP-exposure fractions (Tables 5, 7), child-order regressions (Tables 3, 6), and a propensity-score-matched comparison of clients that disallow ELP routing (Table 9, MatchIt nearest neighbour with date FE only).
design_notes: R scripts Table1.R-Table10.R and Figure1-3.R on parentorders.Rdata and childorders.Rdata (broker parent/child orders, masked ClientID). The causal argument in the abstract uses parent orders of investors that disallow routing to ELPs (Table 9 matching; Table 10 single-client switch).

specs.exclusion_reason: single treated client and single switch date (not staggered); time-varying order-level controls; additional Ticker FE
specs.controls: FracTrBODP FracTrODP FracTrPasLit PartRate InvPrice IvlMidVol FracDur IvlTvr

data_access_note: Proprietary broker order data shipped with masked client identities.
data_provenance_note: Client identities masked (ClientID codes); values appear to be the original order data.
software_notes: R (lfe, MatchIt, stargazer) plus LaTeX for figures.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text; abstract from data/frame/mnsc.jsonl).
